section: 74th Amendment - Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule, types of urban local bodies, ward committees, DPC and MPC
subsections: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included

accepted.s: The Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992, popularly known as the Nagarpalika Act, came into force on which date?
accepted.x: The 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993. 24 April 1993 is associated with the commencement of the 73rd Amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the close-date trap by distinguishing the commencement dates of the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992:
1. It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in December 1992.
2. Presidential assent was given in April 1993.
3. It came into force on 24 April 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993; 24 April 1993 was the commencement date of the 73rd Amendment.
accepted.tq: Separate the passage, assent and commencement dates instead of treating them as one event.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Part of the Constitution was inserted by the Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992?
o: Part X relating to Scheduled and Tribal Areas
Part IXA relating to the Municipalities
accepted.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, titled “The Municipalities”.
accepted.tq: Test the exact constitutional Part and its subject rather than the amendment number alone.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Part IXA of the Constitution, inserted by the 74th Amendment, extends from:
accepted.x: Part IXA, “The Municipalities”, comprises Articles 243P to 243ZG.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise constitutional article range and reject the nearby Part IX range.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 74th Amendment inserted which of the following Schedules in the Constitution?
accepted.x: The 74th Amendment inserted the Twelfth Schedule, which contains 18 municipal functions linked to Article 243W.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-to-Schedule association as a direct constitutional recall question.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional effect of the 74th Amendment?
o: It abolished the distinction among municipal corporations, municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
It made local government a Union List subject and municipalities optional for all States.
It transferred all municipal taxation powers exclusively to the Union Government.
It gave urban local bodies constitutional status and made a uniform municipal framework obligatory for States.
accepted.x: The 74th Amendment gave urban local bodies constitutional status and required States to establish a uniform municipal framework through conforming laws.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the two distinct consequences without adding an extreme claim.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to urban local government in India, consider the following statements:
1. Local Government continues to be a subject in the State List.
2. The 74th Amendment transferred Local Government to the Union List.
3. Municipal laws were required to be brought into conformity with the Constitution within one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Local Government remains in the State List, and Article 243ZF required municipal laws to be brought into conformity within one year. Statement 2 is false because the subject was not transferred to the Union List.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong-list trap and connect Article 243ZF with the one-year compliance requirement.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a compulsory provision to be incorporated in State municipal law under the 74th Amendment?
o: The manner of electing the Mayor
Direct election of all members from wards
Representation of Members of Parliament in municipalities
accepted.x: Direct election of all municipal members from wards is compulsory. Representation of MPs, reservation for backward classes and the manner of electing the Chairperson are left to State legislatures.
accepted.tq: Distinguish mandatory constitutional requirements from provisions left to State legislative choice.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 74th Amendment?
o: Reservation for backward classes in every municipality
Ward Committees in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to population
accepted.x: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary and is left to the State legislature. Ward Committees for municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, five-year terms, and SC/ST reservation are compulsory provisions.
accepted.tq: Find the provision expressly left to State legislative discretion among otherwise mandatory features.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Article)
(a) Article 243Q
(b) Article 243R
(c) Article 243S
(d) Article 243T

List-II (Provision)
(i) Ward Committees
(ii) Reservation of seats
(iii) Types of municipalities
(iv) Composition of municipalities
accepted.x: Article 243Q deals with types of municipalities, Article 243R with their composition, Article 243S with Ward Committees and Article 243T with reservation of seats.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article–subject pairs and eliminate codes that reverse adjacent provisions.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A municipality has a population of 3 lakh. Which constitutional requirement becomes applicable to it under the 74th Amendment?
o: The Mayor must be directly elected by all residents of the State.
A Ward Committee must be constituted.
The municipality must be converted into a Municipal Corporation.
Reservation for backward classes becomes compulsory.
accepted.x: Ward Committees are compulsory in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more. The other consequences do not automatically follow from the population threshold.
accepted.tq: Apply the population threshold in Article 243S to a concrete municipal situation.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding municipal tenure and elections:
1. A municipality has a five-year term.
2. An election must be held within six months of dissolution of a municipality.
3. The State Election Commission is responsible for municipal elections.
4. The State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of municipalities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Articles 243U, 243ZA and 243Y provide the relevant constitutional framework for tenure, elections and financial review.
accepted.tq: Recognize a complete cluster of related compulsory provisions and select the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following matters is voluntary and may be decided by the State legislature under the 74th Amendment?
o: The five-year term of a municipality
The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson
Ward Committees in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more
State Election Commission supervision of municipal elections
accepted.x: The manner of electing the Chairperson or Mayor is left to the State legislature. The other three are compulsory constitutional provisions.
accepted.tq: Use the compulsory-versus-voluntary table to identify the discretionary provision.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

(a) Article 243W — Powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities
(b) Article 243X — State Election Commission
(c) Article 243Y — Ward Committees
(d) Article 243ZF — Reservation of seats
accepted.x: Article 243W concerns municipal powers, authority and responsibilities, including Twelfth Schedule subjects. Articles 243X, 243Y, 243ZF respectively concern municipal taxation and funds, the State Finance Commission, and conformity of existing laws.
accepted.tq: Check the constitutional article attached to each provision and reject swapped article numbers.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Twelfth Schedule contains how many functional items relating to municipalities?
accepted.x: The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 municipal functional items. The Eleventh Schedule, relating to Panchayats, contains 29 subjects.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the numerical count of the Twelfth Schedule from the larger Eleventh Schedule count.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals
accepted.x: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals are Twelfth Schedule subjects. Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical and vocational education are Eleventh Schedule subjects used as distractors.
accepted.tq: Separate municipal Twelfth Schedule functions from Panchayat Eleventh Schedule distractors.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
accepted.x: Libraries and markets and fairs are listed under the Eleventh Schedule, not the Twelfth Schedule. Urban poverty alleviation, urban forestry and environmental protection, and regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries are Twelfth Schedule subjects.
accepted.tq: Use the municipal-versus-Panchayat list distinction to identify the excluded subject.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Twelfth Schedule subject)
(a) Urban and town planning
(b) Water supply
(c) Fire services
(d) Urban poverty alleviation

List-II (Functional group)
(i) Social
(ii) Infrastructure
(iii) Planning
(iv) Infrastructure
accepted.x: Urban and town planning belongs to the Planning group; water supply and fire services are Infrastructure subjects; urban poverty alleviation belongs to the Social group.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive planning and social pairs, then resolve the two infrastructure entries.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Regulation of land use and building construction — Planning
2. Roads and bridges — Infrastructure
3. Public health, sanitation and solid waste management — Health and environment
4. Slum improvement and upgradation — Social
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the functional groups of the Twelfth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Verify each pair against the functional classification rather than relying on a single familiar subject.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following sets consists entirely of Twelfth Schedule subjects relating to amenities and culture?
1. Parks, gardens and playgrounds
2. Cultural, educational and aesthetic aspects
3. Street lighting, parking, bus stops and public conveniences
4. Technical and vocational education
accepted.x: Items 1, 2 and 3 are Twelfth Schedule municipal subjects. Technical and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule subject and is therefore excluded.
accepted.tq: Spot the single Panchayat-list insertion into an otherwise municipal group.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Regulatory group of the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Vital statistics, including registration of births and deaths
accepted.x: Vital statistics, including births and deaths, are included in the Regulatory group. Urban poverty alleviation is a Social subject, urban forestry belongs to Health and environment, and parks and gardens belong to Amenities and culture.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely related functional groups by matching the exact municipal responsibility.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following combinations contains only subjects found in the Eleventh Schedule and NOT in the Twelfth Schedule?
1. Non-conventional energy
2. Small-scale industries
3. Technical and vocational education
4. Public amenities such as street lighting and parking
accepted.x: Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical and vocational education are Eleventh Schedule subjects. Street lighting and parking are Twelfth Schedule municipal amenities.
accepted.tq: Use elimination by separating the three Panchayat subjects from the municipal amenity.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The Twelfth Schedule includes functions relating to urban poverty alleviation.
Reason (R): The Twelfth Schedule is concerned exclusively with physical infrastructure such as roads, bridges and water supply.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: The Assertion is true because urban poverty alleviation is a Twelfth Schedule subject. The Reason is false because the Schedule also covers social, environmental, cultural and regulatory functions, not exclusively physical infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Test the absolute word “exclusively” in the Reason against the wider range of municipal functions.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an environmental function included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Promotion of non-conventional energy in rural areas
Distribution under the Public Distribution System
Urban forestry and protection of the environment and ecology
accepted.x: Urban forestry and protection of the environment and ecology are included in the Twelfth Schedule. The other options are associated with Eleventh Schedule Panchayat subjects or related rural functions.
accepted.tq: Apply the urban qualifier to distinguish the Twelfth Schedule environmental function from rural-list distractors.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
(a) Fire services — Infrastructure
(b) Safeguarding weaker sections, including persons with disabilities — Social
(c) Vital statistics — Regulatory
(d) Slaughter houses and tanneries — Amenities and culture
accepted.x: Slaughter houses and tanneries belong to the Regulatory group, not Amenities and culture. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the functional category of the final item rather than accepting a familiar municipal activity at face value.
accepted.sec: Twelfth Schedule - 18 subjects  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following constitutional developments in chronological order:
A. Commencement of the 73rd Amendment
B. Passage of the 74th Amendment by both Houses
C. Presidential assent to the 74th Amendment
D. Commencement of the 74th Amendment
accepted.x: The 74th Amendment was passed in December 1992, the 73rd Amendment commenced on 24 April 1993, Presidential assent to the 74th Amendment was given in April 1993, and the 74th Amendment commenced on 1 June 1993.
accepted.tq: Place the two commencement dates around the passage and assent events before fixing the final sequence.
accepted.sec: 74th Amendment - commencement, Part inserted, provisions included vs not included  [APPSC]
